description: Remove Extension label from Exercise 23: neutron beta decay and these conservation checks are covered in Section 14.5.

changes.before: <exercise id="fs-id3291026" type="conceptual-questions"><problem id="fs-id3291026-revised-problem"><para id="fs-id3291026-revised-p1"><span id="fs-id3291026-extension"/><emphasis effect="bold">Extension.</emphasis> A free neutron undergoes <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><m:msup><m:mi>β</m:mi><m:mo>−</m:mo></m:msup></m:math> decay: <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><m:mrow><m:mi>n</m:mi><m:mo>→</m:mo><m:mi>p</m:mi><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:msup><m:mi>e</m:mi><m:mo>−</m:mo></m:msup><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:msub><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>ν</m:mi><m:mo>¯</m:mo></m:mover><m:mi mathvariant="italic">e</m:mi></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math>. Check electric charge and nucleon number before and after the decay. Using <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>L</m:mi><m:mi>e</m:mi></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mo>+</m:mo><m:mn>1</m:mn></m:mrow></m:math> for the electron and −1 for the electron antineutrino, check electron-family number as well.</para></problem></exercise>
